to_quote: For a bounded self-adjoint block operator H=[[s,h*],[h,B]], its deleted-site cavity is B. At z=E+i eta with eta>0, define S(z)=<h,(B-z)^(-1)h> and b(E,eta)=eta+Im S(z)>0. For a lattice root, h contains its hopping coefficients. This definition applies to finite and infinite cavities; it does not assert any uniform small-eta lower bound.

rationale: The coupled-limit example uses the same cavity damping in a finite root decomposition.
from_quote: Independent review pending. Let D_N have diagonal grid v_j=-1+(2j+1)/N, let u_N be the normalized all-ones vector, and let B_N,h_N be the cavity blocks in a basis starting with u_N. On J=(-1/2,1/2), eta_N=N^(-1/4), N>=16, the scalar resolvent g_N has Im g_N>=pi/8 and |g_N|<=C+1/4, C=(log3)/2+pi/2. Hence b_N=Im g_N/|g_N|^2>=pi/[8(C+1/4)^2]>0 and its integrated log(1+1/b_N) is uniformly bounded along eta_N. At every fixed N the same functional diverges as eta->0. Thus fixed-size divergence does not force successive limits. This is an abstract finite-cavity example, not an Anderson proof.

For the diagonal operator D delta_x=X_x delta_x on l2(Z3), with iid uniform[-1,1] variables, every realization has site measure delta_(X_x) and a complete eigenbasis. Yet sup_(E real,eta>0) E Im<(delta_0),(D-E-i eta)^(-1)delta_0> <= pi/2 and integral_R Im G00 dE=pi in each sample. Thus these first-moment controls do not imply quenched AC. This refutes a proof implication, not the nearest-neighbor weak-disorder Anderson conjecture.
